migrations.title: The initial Postgres schema (ADR 0005), replacing Firestore.
migrations.description: The initial Postgres schema (ADR 0005), replacing Firestore. ## Why every table is `data jsonb` plus generated columns The obvious port is a typed column per field. It was rejected because the risk here is not query performance, it is *fidelity*: the export bundle must round-trip byte-identically or the migration silently loses data, and a hand-written codec across 21 collections is 21 chances to drop a field. The repository already writes whole documents: `stageNodeUpdate` merges the patch into the record and `set`s all of it, never a partial UPDATE, so a single `jsonb` column matches the existing write model exactly and is lossless by construction. Reads are `JSON.parse` for free (node-postgres hands back a parsed object). The queryable fields are then GENERATED ALWAYS ... STORED columns derived from `data`. They cannot drift from the document because Postgres computes them, and they index like any ordinary column, so the joins and WHERE clauses that Firestore could not do are available: SELECT e.data FROM edges e JOIN nodes n ON n.space = e.space AND n.id = e.src WHERE e.space = $1 AND e.type = 'HELD' AND n.deleted_at IS NULL; ## Timestamps stay TEXT `nowIso()` writes ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds. Those strings sort lexicographically in exactly timestamp order, so `ORDER BY updated_at DESC` and `deleted_at < $cutoff` behave identically to today. Converting to `timestamptz` would buy date arithmetic we do not do, and cost a formatting round-trip that could silently reshape every timestamp in the database. ## Data spaces `demo` is a `space` column (part of every primary key), injected by one query helper. A forgotten filter is a missing-column error rather than a silent data leak.

migrations.title: Generated columns the retention sweep filters on.
migrations.description: Generated columns the retention sweep filters on. `purgeExpiredTrash` deletes every dependent record of a purged node, habit checks, dedup dismissals, by matching a foreign id inside the document. Without these columns those become unindexed jsonb probes, which is fine at today's size and wrong as soon as it is not. Split from 001 rather than folded into it: 001 is already applied, and rewriting an applied migration means the schema on a developer's machine depends on when they last reset it.

migrations.title: `run_id` on meta_runs, for the duplicate-scan results.
migrations.description: `run_id` on meta_runs, for the duplicate-scan results. Firestore modelled a scan as `meta/dedup_scan/runs/{runId}/results/{pair}`. two levels of subcollection. `meta_runs` flattens that: the journal rows and the scan results both hang off a meta document, and `run_id` is what separates one scan's results from the previous one's so a superseded run can be read or discarded as a unit.

migrations.title: Make child tables key on (space, id) like every other table.
migrations.description: Make child tables key on (space, id) like every other table. 001 gave `import_rows`, `import_raw_chunks`, and `meta_runs` a composite key of (space, parent_id, id), mirroring the Firestore path they came from. That reads naturally and is wrong in one specific way: the repository's document helpers upsert with `ON CONFLICT (space, id)`, and Postgres requires the conflict target to match a unique constraint, so every staged import would have failed at runtime with "no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification". Row ids are already globally unique (UUIDs, or derived hashes), so the parent adds nothing to identity. It stays as an indexed foreign key, which is what actually carries the cascade.

migrations.title: Add query columns for the résumé studio without changing document storage.
migrations.description: Add query columns for the résumé studio without changing document storage. Existing rows remain valid: absent JSON keys simply generate NULL.

migrations.title: Cover letters table (SRS FR-RES-020 / §4.5).
migrations.description: Cover letters table (SRS FR-RES-020 / §4.5). Generation UI is deferred; this migration only stands up durable storage so later compile/export work can attach without another schema break. Marked optional in export bundles so older backups remain restorable.

migrations.title: Cloud control plane and workspace partitioning.
migrations.description: Cloud control plane and workspace partitioning. The original `space` column separates one self-hosted owner's real graph from an internal demo. It cannot safely represent customer tenancy: a browser chose it with a request header and it has only two values. This migration keeps that legacy compatibility surface while adding a server-selected `workspace_id` to every durable graph table. Existing data is moved without rewriting its JSON documents: real rows are assigned to the claimable legacy workspace and demo rows to an unassigned system workspace. The application only enters multi-tenant mode when its server flag is enabled, so self-hosted installations continue to work while the hosted rollout is prepared.

migrations.title: Provider timestamps make webhook processing monotonic across retries and delayed delivery.
migrations.description: Provider timestamps make webhook processing monotonic across retries and delayed delivery.

migrations.title: Make the workspace key the actual document identity.
migrations.description: Make the workspace key the actual document identity. Migration 007 added a unique `(workspace_id, id)` index, but leaving the historical `(space, id)` primary key in place would still make singleton documents such as `meta/search_generation` collide between two Cloud workspaces. This promotes the tenant key to every table's primary key and replaces the old child foreign keys with the workspace-aware ones introduced in 007.

migrations.title: Preserve direct legacy `space` inserts while primary keys become workspace based.
migrations.description: Preserve direct legacy `space` inserts while primary keys become workspace based. Repository writes always pass an explicit workspace id; this trigger only repairs old scripts/tests that insert a `demo` row and rely on the old column default.
